s.how: Rub 80g cold butter into 100g plain flour and 100g rolled oats with a pinch of salt. Stir in 80g grated vintage cheddar and 3 tbsp cold milk to form a dough. Roll 5mm thick, cut into 16 squares and prick with a fork. Bake at 180C for 15 minutes until golden, then cool. Top each with a slice of cheddar from 150g, a spoon of tomato chutney and a slice of dill pickle.

s.note: the Lone Islands and their market
s.how: Warm 150g green olives and 150g kalamata olives gently in olive oil with strips of lemon peel, sliced garlic and a pinch of chilli flakes for 5 minutes. Tip into a bowl and serve warm with torn crusty bread for mopping up.

m.note: the long voyage to the edge of the world
m.how: Boil 800g baby potatoes until tender and crush lightly. Pan-fry 4 snapper fillets skin side down until crisp, then flip for a minute. Add butter, lemon juice and capers to the pan and spoon over the fish. Serve with the potatoes.

w.note: the sea of white lilies at the edge of the world
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream and thin slices of white peach like lilies.

d.note: the sweet water near the edge of the world
d.how: Mix the juice of 4 lemons with 100ml elderflower cordial and 700ml cold water in a jug. Peel 1 Lebanese cucumber into long ribbons. Tear a handful of mint into the jug and stir. Fill 4 glasses with ice and cucumber ribbons and pour the lemonade over. Top with a splash of soda water if you want bubbles.
